claims.text: The threshold questions the rider owns are answered on a clean record. The trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip TRP-00535 on a consistent timeline (accepted 06:50:40, started 06:56:40, ended 08:03:40; ledger closed 08:04:00), so the same-trip requirement in POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied. The trace is also complete: 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of the integrity limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 is engaged, no impairment disclosure is owed by either party, and the trace carries its full 1.0 weight into any finding the tribunal makes.

The rider takes the governing measurement and not a flattering one. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs and bars trip_record.actual_distance_km from the threshold test; the trace measures 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km, an excess of 0.25 km, or 1.24% of optimal. Both establishment gates - more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal - therefore fail, and the rider says so plainly: the rider does not contend that a route deviation is established on this trip, and does not seek a POL-RD-02 recomputation of the fare. The rider's complaint is a time complaint, not a kilometre complaint.

The loss the record does establish is the time loss. The fare breakdown bills 67.0 minutes at S$0.28/min (S$18.76) against a booked optimal duration of 44.0 minutes, so 23 minutes of the charge is congested running, and the HIGH-severity accident advisory at EV-ADVIS-00535-01 (two lanes closed, 60 minutes of overlap with the trip window) explains it. That advisory does not, however, do the work the driver's statement asks of it: POL-RD-03 excuses a route only where the actual route leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after, and the trace shows 20.35 km driven against a booked optimal of 20.1 km while the shortest lawful alternative was 22.8 km - the vehicle never left the corridor, so no corridor departure is being excused. The rider accordingly records that its missed train and rebooking cost have no route to recovery under the loaded policy, and asks the tribunal to decide the distance gate on the 0.25 km trace figure alone.

claims.text: There is no route deviation on this trip at all. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is the polyline length in the trace, not the rounded copy on the trip record: the trace measures 20.35 km against a booked optimal of 20.1 km, an excess of 0.25 km, or 1.24%. Both establishment gates must pass and neither does — 0.25 km is not greater than 20% of optimal (4.02 km), and it is not greater than 0.8 km. POL-RD-01 is explicit that if either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The platform's own derived deviation block returns the status 'no deviation' for this trip, with excess_km 0.25 and excess_pct 1.2438%. The threshold and material-threshold fields it applies (0.8 km / 20% and 8.0 km / 50%) are never approached.

Even if any excess survived the gate, it is fully exonerated. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20261435-001 records a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident with two lanes closed on the SLE northbound near Lentor exit; that corridor intersects the route and the advisory window (06:36–07:56) overlaps the trip window (06:56–08:03). On POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured 0.25 km, 1.30 x (22.8 - 20.1) + 1.0 = 4.51 km) = 0.25 km, so the entire measured excess is a justified closure avoidance and nothing is left to refund.

Because the excess is fully exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand — the driver is not at fault for the accident. POL-RD-09(2) confirms that on a POL-RD-03 exoneration the distance and time charges are kept and only off-route ERP is corrected as a pass-through; here the fare breakdown carries 0.00 of ERP and 0.00 of tolls, so there is nothing to correct in any event.

The 67-minute duration against a 44-minute optimal is a traffic-delay effect, not a longer route. The driver's trace, 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps, never leaves the optimal corridor by more than 0.25 km, and the delay window coincides exactly with the accident advisory. Time lost in queued or slow traffic is not excess distance under POL-RD-01, and the rider's claim is built on elapsed time, not on the distance the policy measures.

The closure-adjusted recomputation shown in the fare breakdown's derived block does not generate a refund. POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'; no deviation is established on this trace, and POL-RD-03 fully excuses the only 0.25 km that exists, so the POL-RD-02 arithmetic is not triggered and the metered charge on the ledger stands.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists to uplift anything. On POL-RD-06 the relevant counters are driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, which is 0, against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d, which is 250; that is below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05-ratio test, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift of POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral of POL-RD-06(c) is licensed. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day field this test names and cannot be substituted.

The loss the rider presses — a missed train and roughly $200 of consequential change costs — is not a route-deviation remedy. POL-RD-02 makes any refund arithmetic against the fare breakdown rather than discretionary damages, and the ledger records a metered total charged of SGD 38.66 with no refund issued. A small or large consequential loss outside the fare cannot be recovered through this policy.

This dispute was filed by the rider and the present state is a live charge (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: it leaves that state exactly as it stands, which on a rider-filed claim that the evidence does not support is the driver-favourable outcome and keeps the fare the driver earned.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the dispositive question is the distance the policy measures, and on this trip the answer is that no route deviation exists.

Governing measurement (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00535) records 20.35 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the booked platform optimal on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00535) is 20.1 km. Excess = 0.25 km, which is 1.24% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of the optimal distance. 0.25 km fails both gates. Both parties agree on this, and the policy is explicit that where either gate fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

On the driver's exoneration (POL-RD-03). Because no excess survives the POL-RD-01 gate there is nothing for the closure clause to excuse, so it is not needed to decide this case. For completeness of the record: the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00535-01, SLE northbound near Lentor exit, 06:36-07:56) does overlap the trip window, but the trace shows the vehicle stayed on the booked corridor (20.35 km driven against a 20.1 km optimal, with the shortest lawful alternative being 22.8 km), so the corridor-departure limb of POL-RD-03 is not made out. That does not change the result.

On the rider's time complaint. The ride took 67 minutes against a 44-minute optimal, and the metered charge of SGD 38.66 includes 67.0 minutes at SGD 0.28/min (SGD 18.76). Time lost to congestion is not excess distance under POL-RD-01, and the loaded policy provides no time-only refund. The recomputation figures in the fare ledger (SGD 6.70 computed against the booked optimal, and SGD 6.35 computed against a closure-adjusted optimal of 20.35 km) are conditioned on a deviation being established under POL-RD-01; none is, so neither is applied.

On the roughly SGD 200 of consequential change costs and the missed train. These are not a route-deviation remedy. POL-RD-02 makes any refund arithmetic against the fare breakdown rather than discretionary damages, and no deviation has been established to trigger it.

On billing integrity (POL-RD-09(4)). The fare breakdown carries SGD 0.00 ERP, SGD 0.00 tolls and SGD 0.00 airport surcharge, so there is no phantom gantry or unmatched charge line and no billing-integrity referral arises.

On the repeat-deviation check (POL-RD-06). driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05-ratio test, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift of POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral of POL-RD-06(c) is licensed. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day field this test names and was correctly not substituted for it.

On trace integrity (POL-RD-07). The trace carries 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) is engaged, no impairment discount applies, and no escalation is engaged. All artifacts that carry the deciding facts (EV-GPS-00535 and EV-TRIP-00535) sit at weight 1.0.

Result: NO_ACTION. The fare of SGD 38.66 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) stands as charged; no refund issues to the rider, no compensation issues to the driver, and no clause produces a referral. Confidence 0.95, above the 0.70 floor.

One open question, which belongs here and not in the referrals list because no clause compels it: whether the platform wishes to make a goodwill or service-recovery gesture for the 23 minutes of delay on a journey the driver could not have shortened. The policy does not require it.

This policy measures distance, not time. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement and forbids citing the trip record's rounded copy for the threshold test. The trace (EV-GPS-00535) is complete — 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, full weight 1.0 — and records 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00535). That is an excess of 0.25 km, or 1.24% of optimal. A deviation is established only where the excess is both greater than 0.8 km absolute and greater than 20% of optimal. 0.25 km fails both gates, so no route deviation exists and the metered charge stands. I note that both advocates reached this same conclusion from the same trace figure; the rider does not contend a deviation is established and does not seek a distance recomputation.

The rider's genuine loss here is time and money outside the fare: the trip ran 67.0 minutes against a booked optimal of 44.0 minutes, and the rider missed a train and incurred roughly SGD 200 of rebooking costs. POL-RD-02 makes any remedy arithmetic against the fare breakdown rather than discretionary damages, and the loaded policy contains no route by which a missed connection or consequential rebooking cost can be recovered from the platform or the driver. I have no power to award them, and the platform's voucher offers are outside this ruling's scope. The 23 minutes of extra running time is congestion, not extra distance; POL-RD-01 does not measure it.

The driver's alternative argument — that the LTA accident advisory EV-ADVIS-00535-01 (HIGH severity, two lanes closed on SLE northbound near Lentor, active 06:36–07:56, overlapping the trip window 06:56–08:03) would exonerate any excess under POL-RD-03 — is moot, because there is no excess to exonerate. I record only that the advisory is present in the pool and covers the trip window, so no escalation arises on that account under POL-RD-10(5), and POL-RD-09(2) would preserve the distance and time charges in any event. The fare breakdown carries 0.00 of ERP and 0.00 of tolls and no airport surcharge, so there is nothing to correct under POL-RD-09 and no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4).

I checked the driver profile as POL-RD-06 requires. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither the 3-flag test nor the 0.05-ratio test is met: no repeat-deviation pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift, and no conduct referral. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day field that test names (POL-GEN-01), and it changes nothing here.

The rider filed this dispute and the charge is live (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed claim leaves that state exactly as it stands. No escalation trigger in POL-RD-10 fires: the identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, the timestamps are consistent, the invoked advisory is present and in-window, and no refund or unmatched charge line exists.

Confidence is 0.95. The deciding fact — that the excess falls below both POL-RD-01 gates — is carried by artifacts at full weight 1.0 (the trace, the trip record and the advisory), so nothing pulls the cap below the 0.70 floor.

The clause measures excess as actual distance minus optimal distance and makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure; trip_record.actual_distance_km (20.4 km) is a rounded copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test. Both establishment gates must pass and neither does: 0.25 km is far below the 0.8 km absolute gate and far below the 20% gate (4.02 km). POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. Both advocates reached this conclusion independently and I accept it.

The rider's real complaint is time, not distance. The ride took 67.0 minutes against a 44.0-minute optimal estimate (the fare bills 67.0 minutes at SGD 0.28/min = SGD 18.76). POL-RD-01 measures distance; time lost to queued or slow traffic is not excess distance, and no clause in the loaded policy makes congested running time refundable. The rider's own advocate accepts that the missed train and the roughly SGD 200 of rebooking cost have no route to recovery under this policy.

Exculpatory clauses (POL-RD-03) do not change the result. The driver cites the LTA accident advisory (EV-ADVIS-00535-01: two lanes closed, SLE northbound near Lentor, window 06:36–07:56 overlapping the trip window). Because no excess survives the POL-RD-01 gate, there is nothing for POL-RD-03 to excuse. In any event the rider is right that limb (c) is not met: the 20.35 km actually driven stayed within the 20.1 km corridor while the shortest lawful alternative was 22.8 km, so the vehicle never left and rejoined the optimal corridor.

POL-RD-02 does not run. It applies only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it. With no deviation established the arithmetic is not triggered; the derived refund figures carried inside the fare breakdown's money block are therefore non-operative and the metered charge stands.

Pass-through lines (POL-RD-09). The fare breakdown carries SGD 0.00 of ERP and SGD 0.00 of tolls and no off-route gantry lines, so there is nothing to correct. The billing-integrity limb POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom charge.

Party-relative outcome (POL-GEN-03). This is a rider-filed dispute and the present state is a live charge (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00); NO_ACTION leaves that state exactly as it stands.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute, and the evidence does not show a route deviation, so the charge stands unchanged (NO_ACTION).

On the measurement the two sides agree. POL-RD-01 measures the route on the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: EV-GPS-00535 records 20.35 km against a booked optimal of 20.1 km on EV-TRIP-00535 — an excess of 0.25 km, or 1.24%. A deviation is established only if the excess is both greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal. It is neither, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The platform's own derived deviation block says the same ('no deviation'; 0.25 km / 1.2438%).

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 is never triggered and no distance-or-time refund arises. For transparency: the fare is a metered SGD 38.66 (base 3.80 + distance 15.30 for 20.4 km + time 18.76 for 67 min + platform fee 0.80), internally consistent. The record also carries a POL-RD-02 recomputation that would yield 6.70 against the booked optimal, and 6.35 against a closure-adjusted optimal, but neither applies. ERP and tolls are 0.00 and no airport surcharge applies, so there is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4).

The driver's fallback under POL-RD-03 is not reached, because exoneration only matters where there is excess to exonerate, and there is none; in any event POL-RD-03 requires the route to leave the optimal corridor and rejoin it, which a 20.35 km drive against a 20.1 km optimal (with a 22.8 km lawful alternative available) does not show. The LTA accident advisory EV-ADVIS-00535-01 (HIGH severity, two lanes closed, 60 minutes overlapping the trip window) explains the delay, not any detour.

The rider's real loss is time and its consequences: 67 minutes charged against a 44-minute estimate, a missed train, and roughly SGD 200 of changes. This policy compensates a longer route, not a slower one, and POL-RD-02 makes any refund arithmetic on the fare breakdown rather than discretionary damages; consequential losses such as the missed train are not recoverable here. The platform's voucher offers fall outside this ruling.

No repeat-deviation uplift or conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, below both POL-RD-06 tests. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the field POL-RD-06 names and was not used; no other profile field decided anything in this case.

The trace is clean (403 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps), so POL-RD-07 does not impair it and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger — including the 0.70 confidence floor — fires. Confidence 0.95, within the 1.0 cap set by the two artifacts (both weight 1.0) that carry the deciding measurement.

Outcome: the fare of SGD 38.66 remains charged; no refund and no driver compensation.

ledger.claim: The threshold questions the rider owns are answered on a clean record. The trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip TRP-00535 on a consistent timeline (accepted 06:50:40, started 06:56:40, ended 08:03:40; ledger closed 08:04:00), so the same-trip requirement in POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied. The trace is also complete: 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of the integrity limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 is engaged, no impairment disclosure is owed by either party, and the trace carries its full 1.0 weight into any finding the tribunal makes.

The rider takes the governing measurement and not a flattering one. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs and bars trip_record.actual_distance_km from the threshold test; the trace measures 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km, an excess of 0.25 km, or 1.24% of optimal. Both establishment gates - more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal - therefore fail, and the rider says so plainly: the rider does not contend that a route deviation is established on this trip, and does not seek a POL-RD-02 recomputation of the fare. The rider's complaint is a time complaint, not a kilometre complaint.

The loss the record does establish is the time loss. The fare breakdown bills 67.0 minutes at S$0.28/min (S$18.76) against a booked optimal duration of 44.0 minutes, so 23 minutes of the charge is congested running, and the HIGH-severity accident advisory at EV-ADVIS-00535-01 (two lanes closed, 60 minutes of overlap with the trip window) explains it. That advisory does not, however, do the work the driver's statement asks of it: POL-RD-03 excuses a route only where the actual route leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after, and the trace shows 20.35 km driven against a booked optimal of 20.1 km while the shortest lawful alternative was 22.8 km - the vehicle never left the corridor, so no corridor departure is being excused. The rider accordingly records that its missed train and rebooking cost have no route to recovery under the loaded policy, and asks the tribunal to decide the distance gate on the 0.25 km trace figure alone.

There is no route deviation on this trip at all. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is the polyline length in the trace, not the rounded copy on the trip record: the trace measures 20.35 km against a booked optimal of 20.1 km, an excess of 0.25 km, or 1.24%. Both establishment gates must pass and neither does — 0.25 km is not greater than 20% of optimal (4.02 km), and it is not greater than 0.8 km. POL-RD-01 is explicit that if either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The platform's own derived deviation block returns the status 'no deviation' for this trip, with excess_km 0.25 and excess_pct 1.2438%. The threshold and material-threshold fields it applies (0.8 km / 20% and 8.0 km / 50%) are never approached.

Even if any excess survived the gate, it is fully exonerated. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20261435-001 records a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident with two lanes closed on the SLE northbound near Lentor exit; that corridor intersects the route and the advisory window (06:36–07:56) overlaps the trip window (06:56–08:03). On POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured 0.25 km, 1.30 x (22.8 - 20.1) + 1.0 = 4.51 km) = 0.25 km, so the entire measured excess is a justified closure avoidance and nothing is left to refund.

Because the excess is fully exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand — the driver is not at fault for the accident. POL-RD-09(2) confirms that on a POL-RD-03 exoneration the distance and time charges are kept and only off-route ERP is corrected as a pass-through; here the fare breakdown carries 0.00 of ERP and 0.00 of tolls, so there is nothing to correct in any event.

The 67-minute duration against a 44-minute optimal is a traffic-delay effect, not a longer route. The driver's trace, 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps, never leaves the optimal corridor by more than 0.25 km, and the delay window coincides exactly with the accident advisory. Time lost in queued or slow traffic is not excess distance under POL-RD-01, and the rider's claim is built on elapsed time, not on the distance the policy measures.

The closure-adjusted recomputation shown in the fare breakdown's derived block does not generate a refund. POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'; no deviation is established on this trace, and POL-RD-03 fully excuses the only 0.25 km that exists, so the POL-RD-02 arithmetic is not triggered and the metered charge on the ledger stands.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists to uplift anything. On POL-RD-06 the relevant counters are driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, which is 0, against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d, which is 250; that is below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05-ratio test, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift of POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral of POL-RD-06(c) is licensed. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day field this test names and cannot be substituted.
